03 — project

AstroLink

A platform for astronauts to plan their daily routine, design their habitat, and stay connected with family through real-time chat during a mission.

Category

Scheduling · real-time chat

Audience

Astronauts on long-duration missions

My role

Solo build

The problem

Life on a long-duration space mission runs on structure — every hour of work, exercise, and rest is planned in advance — but that same isolation makes it easy to lose touch with the people back home. Astronauts need tools that handle both: the operational side of the mission, and the human side of staying connected.

The approach

AstroLink splits into two connected pieces. Mission Control is where an astronaut plans their day and living space: a Daily Routine planner for structuring work, rest, and exercise, and a Habitat Visualizer for designing and reviewing their living quarters. Stellar Bridge is the communication layer — a real-time chat space for staying in touch with family and crew, built so a conversation feels immediate rather than like sending a delayed transmission.

What it does

  • Lets astronauts build and adjust their daily work/rest schedule
  • Visualizes and helps design their habitat layout
  • Provides real-time chat to stay connected with family during the mission

Why it matters

The interesting design problem here was treating operational planning and personal connection as equally important, rather than building a mission-ops tool and bolting on a chat feature as an afterthought — the two are given the same weight because both genuinely affect how a long mission is experienced.
